questions.question: A balloon is rubbed on dry hair and becomes negatively charged. Explain, in terms of electrons, what happened to the balloon and the hair.
questions.expected_answer: Electrons were transferred from the hair to the balloon. The balloon gained electrons and became negative; the hair lost electrons and became positive. No charge was created; it was moved.

questions.question: Explain why a charged balloon sticks to a neutral wall.
questions.expected_answer: The negative balloon repels electrons in the wall's surface slightly away, leaving the nearby surface slightly positive (induced charge). The attraction to the nearer positive region is stronger than the repulsion from the more distant negative region, so the balloon is attracted.

questions.question: Give three safety rules for a thunderstorm, with a reason for one of them.
questions.expected_answer: Go indoors into a solid building or a car with a metal roof; avoid tall isolated trees, open fields, water and metal fences; do not use corded phones or showers. E.g. a metal car body conducts the current around the occupants into the ground; trees are tall and attract strikes.
